sandbox.description: Kernel gate for commands. "static": seccomp deny filter (io_uring, ptrace, mount/namespace, bpf, kexec, keyctl). "fence": static + Landlock allowlist -- workspace roots and /tmp-style scratch read-write, system dirs read-only, everything else (including home dirs: `cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa` fails) unreachable, TCP bind blocked where the Landlock ABI supports it. Allowlist-only: workspace.deny is NOT expressible in "fence". "gate": fence (on Landlock-capable hosts) + USER_NOTIF supervisor enforcing the workspace boundary in-kernel (trap set covers every syscall that can write/create/alias/truncate/egress -- openat/openat2/creat, truncate, unlink/unlinkat/rmdir, mkdir/mkdirat/mknod/mknodat, symlink/symlinkat, link/linkat, rename/renameat/renameat2, connect/sendto/sendmsg/sendmmsg, execve -- so legacy-syscall bypasses are impossible; writes/unlinks outside roots and deny-listed paths are blocked, SANDBOX_GATE hooks may approve per-operation; outbound connect/sendto/sendmsg blocked, execve audit-logged). The deny list is write-integrity only: reads of deny-listed paths inside roots are ungated in EVERY mode (`cat .env` works); unlike the file tools, where workspace.deny also blocks reads. Linux x86_64 only; fails at startup when unavailable. Does not restrict network for "static". Comparison table: docs/config-reference.md.
